Contract lens is clean across every check. Summary of what I verified: - **Diff surface**: only `bot/src/index.js`, `bot/test/tick.test.js`, `bot/README.md` (+79/-3). No `docker-compose.yml`, `laya/**`, Dockerfile, CI or `package.json`/`package-lock.json` changes. - **Env vars**: no new `process.env` read is added. Every var the bot reads (`MC_HOST`, `MC_PORT`, `BOT_USERNAME`, `BOT_FOLLOW`, `BRAIN_TICK_MS`, `BRAIN_URL`, `BRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS`) is still passed by `docker-compose.yml:86-92`. Nothing is renamed. - **Secrets/privacy**: grepped every added line for IPs, URLs, domains, `api_key`/`token`/`secret`/`password` — none. Test fixture uses `Steve`. PR #25 body is also clean and says so explicitly. - **Deploy contract**: image stays `ghcr.io/korjavin/idkcraft`; CI tags by `git rev-parse HEAD:bot`, and since `bot/` changed the tree hash changes, so a new image is built and the `deploy` branch rewrite still matches. `bot/Dockerfile` copies only `src/`, so the new test file cannot affect the image build. - **Dependencies**: no new `require()` in the diff; no lockfile change needed. - **Stub-brain start**: `brain.js` and `makeBrain(process.env)` are untouched; the bot still joins with no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. The paused branch skips `brain.decide` entirely rather than changing the `laya` REST shape. - **Loop liveness** (the one critical-severity shape in this lens): the paused early `return` sits inside the `try`, so the `finally` at `bot/src/index.js:120-123` still runs `scheduleNext(lastVisible)` — the tick loop cannot stall on the new path, and every new call (`buildState`, `makeScout`, `pathfinder.stop`) is guarded and inside the existing catch. findings.title: Paused branch ticks the scout even with no player online, unlike the idle branch
findings.body:
The paused block runs the scout seam unconditionally (lines 64-65), outside the `if (target) / else` above it, whereas the normal path only reaches the scout seam after `if (!target) return ...` (lines 79-95) — i.e. scout never scans when nobody is online. `bot/test/tick.test.js:220` pins that invariant for the unpaused path ("never scans or chats when no player is online").

Trigger: a player says `stop` (paused = true), then everyone logs off. `findTarget` returns null, so `lastVisible` is false and the loop settles into the slow 10 s poll — but every one of those ticks still creates the scout (registry is present after spawn) and calls `scout.tick()`, which runs `bot.findBlocks` and `bot.chat('iron_ore x1 at ...')` on an empty server, plus a `scout ...` console line, indefinitely. The unpaused bot does none of this in the same situation.

The root cause is that the paused block is a hand-copy of the idle cost-guard block (lines 79-95) with the scout seam spliced in at a different nesting level; the two copies have already diverged in the diff that introduced them.
findings.fix: Move lines 64-65 inside the `if (target)` arm of the paused block so the scout only ticks when a player is visible, matching the unpaused path.

findings.title: New paused test never exercises the scout seam, the one thing the bead says pausing must preserve
findings.body:
The bead's design is explicit that "the tick still runs perception (scout keeps reporting)" while parked — that separation is the stated learning point. The new test builds a bare `mockBot()` (line 241) with no `registry`, no `findBlocks` and no `blockAt`, so `ctx.scout` is never created and `ctx.scout.tick()` is never called on any paused tick. Deleting lines 64-65 of `bot/src/index.js` — the scout seam inside the paused branch — leaves the whole suite green, so the bot silently stops reporting ore the moment anyone says `stop` and nothing catches it.

The rest of the test is sound: removing the `if (ctx.paused)` block does fail it (the brain would be called and a goal set on the paused ticks).
findings.fix: Use the existing `scoutBot()` helper from the `scout seam` describe (or an inline equivalent) in the paused test and assert `bot.findCalls > 0` / a chat line after a paused tick with a player nearby.

Both checks done: the paused branch does scout with nobody online, and the paused test never touches the scout seam. Finding 1 holds, but its "chats indefinitely" claim is overstated — a parked bot exhausts new veins after the first scan; what persists is a `findBlocks` scan every 10 s plus veins silently marked seen. Finding 2 holds as written: `mockBot()` has no `registry`/`findBlocks`, so `ctx.scout` is never created on the paused path, and the profile treats a missing assertion for new branching logic as a finding.
